chunks.content: 96 Stuffing is for turkeys, not seller notes. Hi Sara, Most buyers think of promissory notes as one static document. But in real deals? They’re more like duct tape. Flexible, essential, and way more effective when used right. Let’s say you’ve got a $5M deal, SBA financing, and a seller willing to carry part of the price. Here’s what usually happens: One note One structure One-size-fits-nobody Instead, you could: Use one note for the 10% retention adjustment Use a second note for the rest Standby on one or both, or whatever is needed Amortization can be different Stretch the term or add flexibility based on what actually helps the business Notes don’t need to be uniform. They need to be useful. Every promissory note should answer one question: “What happens if I don’t get paid?” And every smart seller (or buyer) should understand their answer before signing anything. Got a note term you're stuck on? Send it my way. I’ve probably seen worse.
